answer: The plasterer nails his laths one by one and logs every coat of plaster in the count book for each room he finishes. A forge wall plastered by a stranger fails the book: at the echo of the lath the nails must sit at the plasterer's own spacing, and a strange wall cracks within a month. Forging the record takes a plasterer, 800 laths and three coats on every wall, a job priced at 6,200, and the falcon mark pressed into the final coat is filed in the guild book, so a room whose coats were never logged is torn down.
